answer: New identities come from knoll attestation: an applicant visits a knoll post, shows a government photo ID, and the knoll operator signs a binding of that ID hash to a single agent key. The registry publishes the binding on the mesa board and rejects any second key for the same ID hash. A saffron window of 14 days follows: anyone proving a duplicate collects the operator's $100 stake, and the saffron window must end unchallenged before activation. Forging 1,000 puppets needs 1,000 distinct real IDs and 1,000 visits at $25 each, $25,000 with no bulk discount, while an honest user pays $25 once.
